lines.para: They arrive with the British, from the 1840s. Most are Jewish merchants from Baghdad who came by way of Bombay: the Sassoons, then the Kadoories. They trade in cotton and opium, then invest in property and electricity.
In 1902, the Sassoon brothers give the small community a synagogue on the heights of Mid-Levels. They name it Ohel Leah, “Leah’s tent”, after their mother.
The Kadoories build a club where people meet in the evening to dine, read the London papers and play cards. In 1928, their company opens the Peninsula in Kowloon, a hotel soon famous throughout Asia.
In the 1930s, other Jews arrive, driven out of Europe or Russia, often penniless.
The community stays tiny, a few hundred people. But its great families are among the richest in the colony.
